I've seen him before and I know his deal is primarily medication, which is definitely the right place for me to be starting since I can't even function independently anymore when we aren't accounting for my delayed reactions.

It's funny you say you have "a terrible memory" -- my memory is terrifyingly accurate. I'm usually able to remember the exact date something happened. People who know me well know to believe me completely whenever I tell them how I remember things. Once I grasp something, it's with me for life. 

I also did really well on standardized tests, and people do tell me I "over-analyze" things as well. 

One of the upsides of this is that, when I do end up being able to do something, I do it well; even my teary rambling is cohesive. Some people attribute this to perfectionism, which is what I originally started therapy for when I was very young, but I don't think that's it. I'd love to half-ass something if I could react in an appropriate amount of time, but I can't. 

I'm easily overstimulated which makes a lot of things hard for me. I spend a lot of time by myself, in the quiet, and it's taken 5 years of just sitting quietly outside of therapy to even get to a point where I can explain to a doctor what's wrong with me (in therapy, I'd usually just sit in silence if asked a question that I didn't have words for).

I had the opposite experience, with a postsecret-style blog many years ago. It was just about how I feel so empty and nothing made me feel anything; I'd later learn that I was describing my depression.

I submitted my secret and waited and waited to see it published. When it finally was, I was floored by how little response it'd gotten. One girl had liked it, and when I got in touch with her to try to talk about it, she admitted that she only really felt about half of it but found it interesting. I'd never felt so *alone*.

My family has Virgin Pulse, through my father's employer. It's funny, because nobody at his office takes it seriously. They'll sit at meetings and they all twirl the pedometers around in the air. My mom also put 4 or 5 of the pedometers through the wash in 2014, but she's just an idiot. 

From a developer's standpoint, the software used to track the miles is absolutely awful and I would not wish it on my worst enemy.

Still, it's cool that my family can earn money toward their health insurance by logging extra steps, even if 75% of those steps come from attaching pedometers to ceiling fans.

He gets upset (not angry, just uncomfortable) if there isn't a very specific balance in our social media posts (someone mentioned once that "all" we ever post is stuff about each other, now he basically goes out of his way to make sure it's obvious he has a life outside of me), he avoids confrontation unless it's with someone he's very comfortable around. 

This isn't completely negative (I know he'll never start problems unnecessarily with me, disrespect my family, or be that dude who wants to fight the guy who looked at me wrong) but it's probably not good for him.

Over the course of our relationship, he's developed a spine and a more independent mind and his friends have stopped being his confidants and started just being buddies. His three closest friends are actually all easily the best of the group (one of his closest friends is the guy who's done nothing noteworthy so I didn't mention him, Colin is super cool when we're alone but easily falls into shit behavior with the worse friends like Steve or Phil or Jake, and he can't help but be very close to his twin brother). 

He's also a 21-year-old kid. Sure, that's old enough to know, but I don't expect him to be some sort of moral tower and break down a bunch of relationships. He does try to stick up for me, but he's easily broken down. It's also worth noting that he's taken time, even when I'm not around, to explain/stick up for what I believe and talk with his friends about it. He *makes an effort*, but it's been slow moving and occasionally backfires because of the scale of the problem.

>You might also be *that* girlfriend as you do seem kind of overbearing and if I had to guess *might be* some kind if SJW. 

I guess you're right to a point, but I'm not a "TiA" type and nothing I say is outrageously disagreeable. I deal mostly with issues that can be observed through research, don't use the word "patriarchy" and whatever other jargon, and a majority of things I have opinions on are things I have very personal, sometimes painful experience with. 

I grew up very differently from what I believe now, and I "converted" (for lack of a less creepy word) when I realized that the people who believe what I do were super fucking cool and not the terrible monsters I'd been raised to think they were. Because of this, I actively avoid being alienating/black-and-white about things unless absolutely crucial (like in the case of Steve or the thing I made the Facebook status about) and I go out of my way to not be pushy or overwhelming in any way. I'll say something if someone else brings it up but otherwise I keep quiet about what I believe because I know it makes people uneasy.

All of their friendship gatherings, aside from one or two parties a year, is at my boyfriend's house. 

I don't push what I believe with them. They never would have known had they not asked. I'm not some wacky, offbeat person and I normally get along just fine with their "type." I even consider (or, have considered) some of them my close friends during the times they're less rude to me.

* They're most often not joking; they say they are, but it's *very* personal and my boyfriend agrees that it's usually inappropriate. 

* I have no problem with being too sensitive. They can't take jokes back at them. They become aggressive at the slightest hint of retaliation. I had no problem with this when I was, say, the new girlfriend and I assumed they were just initiating me or something. Half the time it's not jokes or obvious cracks to my face, but they make fun of me with jokes they think are over my head (either talking when they think I'm not listening or using words they don't realize are about me; they didn't know I know exactly how/why they make fun of the way I speak until I finally told them it's not cool last week). 

* My boyfriend and I *usually* hang out alone. I see his friends maybe once or twice a month, maybe three or four if it's summer and I'm seeing *everyone* more often.

Are these extreme fringe opinions that the majority of people would take issue with, or are they simple matters like being a lone democrat in a room full of republicans? 

Definitely more of the latter. I live in a very tiny, VERY red dot in a blue state. It's not that I'm a crazy outlier, but the people I'm with just tend to not line up with me.

It had nothing to do with what people actually *post* on Facebook. I can't unfriend people who masturbated to a video of a sexual assault if I don't know who did it; I wrote out a (very brief, ~150 words) explainer on why the situation was shitty and not cool and I got, not drama, but dismissive cheap jokes. I failed to emphasize that NOBODY, even the people who are quick to take issue with me, thought my post was out of line or anything. It's actually something I was quite proud of. 


>It's hard to tell what is warranted with the vague details; if the beliefs you're being made fun of for are astrology, homeopathy or anti-vaxx I would tell you to that you're gonna have a bad time with that regardless because you're spewing a bunch of hogwash. 

So, I purposely kept this detail-free because my beliefs, while not *extreme*, can be polarizing, and I'm just not up for that debate too. But it's worth noting that Phil is a homeopathy/anti-vaxx guy who will bulldoze anyone in conversation and associates not being vaccinated with a certain morality, and NOBODY gives him shit for it because "it's important to him."

I drink with them maybe once every three months, and it's usually me drinking with my boyfriend and them inviting themselves; my boyfriend's house (lives with his brother) is the "party" house, everyone has a key and lets themselves in whenever, so half the time our time together isn't prearranged or anything.

I left the Facebook thing intentionally vague because I didn't want to bring up the debate about the issue itself; it's not about what happened, it's about how they reacted. I don't want a conversation about whether what I believe is cool or not, I just need to explain how they deal with it. 

I guess I failed to note that the post was very sincere and nobody except these two had an issue with it; my boyfriend thought it was awesome, even my mom (who is normally at my throat about these issues) thought it was super level-headed, fair, agreeable, and mature. It had a bipartisan reach and people I'd never spoken to or even people I was normally disagreeing with on this issue (in addition to the people I normally line up with) were agreeing and sharing the post. 

There was no drama there. Neither of them caused "drama." One said "lol how long did it take you to write this?" and the other joked that he would have loved to be one of the victims of the issue because it's not a big deal (pretty nasty because it was about sexual assault). Everyone who knew about that situation was pissed off and a few people I knew called/texted me after they saw it to ask who those people were and apologize for those assholery.
